overview: Paramedics give advanced emergency care on the way to the hospital: cardiac care, airway management, medications and fast decisions in unsafe places. They coordinate with EMTs, police and emergency room staff. O*NET rates critical thinking at 3.75 out of 5 for this job and active listening at 3.62. Most paramedics complete a vocational program or associate degree after EMT certification. The BLS May 2025 median is $60,600 across 100,610 jobs. The work is physical and outdoors in all weather, with long shifts and real exposure to infection, but many paramedics value the variety and the chance to help.
pay: Paramedic pay depends heavily on location. The median is $60,600, and the top 10% earn $84,850 or more. Washington stands out with a state median of $104,310, 72% above the national figure, followed by New Jersey at $86,630. Texas has the most jobs, 8,410, at a median of $57,500.

faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $60,600 a year. The lowest 10% earn under $44,230 and the top 10% earn $84,850 or more, often with overtime. Washington, New Jersey and Hawaii pay the most, while West Virginia ($48,460) and Oklahoma ($46,790) have the lowest state medians.

faq.q: How do you become a paramedic?
faq.a: You first certify as an EMT, then finish a paramedic program, usually 1 to 2 years at a community college or technical school, and pass a national exam and state license. O*NET places the job in Job Zone 3, which means vocational training or an associate degree.

It is demanding. In O*NET work context data, paramedics rank above 99% of U.S. jobs for long hours and above 98% for working outdoors in all weather. You face exposure to infection and mistakes can have serious consequences, so good teamwork and rest between shifts matter.

faq.q: What can paramedics do next in their careers?
faq.a: Nursing is the most common move. Registered Nurses are an 82% match and earn $97,550, 61% more than paramedics, according to BLS May 2025 data. Respiratory Therapists are an 84% match and earn $82,280, or 36% more, after an associate degree program.
